name: Delaiah
overview: Delaiah is a male figure mentioned in the book of Jeremiah, identified specifically as the son of Shemaiah. He is noted for his role as an official, indicating a position of responsibility or authority during the time of the prophet Jeremiah. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded for him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Delaiah means 'YHWH draws up [like water in a bucket],' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's active involvement. This meaning highlights a connection to God's providential care, although the name was not given directly by God according to the record in Jeremiah 36:12.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Delaiah is the son of Shemaiah, as noted in Jeremiah 36:12. Beyond this father-son relationship, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Delaiah's significance in the biblical narrative arises from his identification as an official during the time of Jeremiah, suggesting involvement in the political or administrative affairs of Judah. His mention in Jeremiah 36:12 situates him within the historical context of Jeremiah's prophetic ministry, providing insight into the individuals connected to the unfolding events of that period.
